narrowResearchQuestion: For the frozen fourteen-take CooperScene release, a model-payload set, and an admissible class of Iperf-to-model workload transport maps, determine which deadline-completion verdicts are invariant across every admissible map and which are only partially or not identified.
defensibleNoveltyBoundary: A CooperScene-release-specific, machine-checkable finite-release identification certificate with sharp lower and upper bounds plus executable endpoint witness transport maps.

occupiedMethodSpace.boundary: Packet size, priority, timing, concurrency, and workload effects on C-V2X are already established.
Workload-transfer bias in cellular replay is already an explicit systems result.
Partial identification itself is not novel.

directlyIdentified: Fourteen official MCAP objects, twelve directed throughput topics, their summary timestamps, and message counts.
Take 9's 1,932 decoded Vector3.x values and approximately 100 ms observation grid.
Receiver-interval throughput under the collection Iperf workload.
conditionallyIdentified: Isolated-transfer deadline completion only after payload, service mapping, queue policy, and endpoint-support rules are fixed.
notIdentified: Periodic-message queue evolution and FIFO, latest-only, or drop semantics.
Final serialized wire bytes and fragmentation or reassembly.
forbiddenInference: Success probability outside the fourteen released takes.
Deployment-population confidence intervals or physical-radio guarantees.

criticalWorkloadMismatch.collectionWorkload: Four agents simultaneously ran Iperf2 UDP clients at 5 Mbps with 100 ms reports.
criticalWorkloadMismatch.modelPayloadExperiment: Model data were sent sequentially in 2100-byte chunks at 1 ms intervals.
criticalWorkloadMismatch.verdict: Directly integrating the Iperf throughput as a fluid service curve for model payloads is an identity-map sensitivity analysis, not a valid point identification of model-traffic transport.

minimumUnblockEvidence: Decode all 73,879 directed throughput messages across all fourteen takes and retain take, receiver, sender, timestamp, and raw x-y-z without imputing take 1's nonuniform channel counts.
Freeze the official inventory, object metadata, parser hashes, CRC results, and exact retrieval manifest.
Establish full-versus-preview payload parity for every take if preview files are used.
Obtain or independently reproduce the Iperf command, version, datagram size, topology, interval statistic, and offered-versus-received-goodput definition.
Obtain raw Table 2 transport logs or run a separately labeled paired MK6 calibration campaign for Iperf and model workloads.
Instrument final serialized bytes, packetization, concurrency, and queue semantics for every named model.

preregisteredEstimand.target: For payload B, deadline d, take t, directed link l, eligible start k, and admissible map g, estimate the finite-release completion indicator and its minimum and maximum over all admissible g and payload bounds.
preregisteredEstimand.commonSupport: Use only start points with a complete deadline observation window and keep a common denominator.
preregisteredEstimand.censoring: Use capped or restricted completion time at a fixed horizon; never report completed-only median or p95 as the primary estimand.
mapClasses: G_release: reproduces observed Iperf workload only and is expected to yield a wide or fully ambiguous interval.
G_calibrated: adds only cumulative-service, concurrency, and packetization bounds supported by paired calibration.
G_identity, constant 1.6 Mbps, and per-link mean: point sensitivity baselines only.
preregisteredEstimand.inference: Primary outputs are deterministic interval containment, pairwise-difference intervals, sharpness, and endpoint witness replay. Frame or link rows are not independent population samples.

positiveControls: The constant 1.6 Mbps path reproduces 8B/1.6 completion time.
Completion is monotone in payload size and deadline.
Identity-map compatibility reproduces the frozen take 9 pilot.
negativeControls: A payload above every available service bound never completes.
Changing Vector3.y or z cannot affect an x-only analysis.
Missing workload-map evidence returns non-identified instead of a default estimate.
Relabeling directed links cannot change a deliberately pooled aggregate.
killCriteria: All fourteen payload streams cannot be decoded.
No empirically justified workload-transfer restriction exists; retain only a non-identification audit.
Serialized-byte bounds cannot be verified; remove named-model ordering claims.
Every preregistered target remains fully ambiguous and every difference interval contains zero.
An endpoint bound cannot emit a feasible witness whose forward replay matches the target within one byte and one nanosecond.

timeline.twoWeekMinimum: Complete all-take decoding, preview parity, preregistration, G_release, any evidence-supported G_calibrated class, witnesses, controls, and a finite-release report. A rigorous non-identification certificate is an acceptable outcome.
timeline.sixToEightWeekFull: Add raw logs or paired physical calibration, serializer instrumentation, nested map classes, agent-setting concurrency, holdout calibration, independent witness replay, and a machine-readable certificate. Do not add perception metrics without a reliable frame sidecar.

topRejectionRisks: Treating sustained 5 Mbps Iperf UDP traffic as transport for a 2100-byte-per-millisecond model workload.
Treating starts, links, or surrogate seeds from one short collection campaign as independent population samples.
Leaving payload, queue, and wire semantics unspecified so the bounds become assumption-driven or methodologically trivial.
panelEntryRequirements: Value-level decoding is complete for all fourteen takes.
The primary admissible map class is separated from point sensitivity baselines.
Payload and queue semantics are frozen.
Sharp bounds and endpoint witnesses pass an independent replay audit.
Every title and claim remains limited to the exact frozen finite release.
